title: Der Vierundzwanzigste
desc: Nine people, real candles, and a bucket
setting: A living room in Kriens at six in the evening, a tree with actual fire on it, and the lights going off.

steps.speaker: Selina
steps.es: Für jeden etwas Kleines. Zwanzig Franken.
steps.en: Something small for everybody. Twenty francs.

options.feedback: It is not. A present that is too big makes pressure, and everybody at that table knows the number.
Nine people and a ceiling. That is the whole brief and it is a kindness to be given it.

options.es: Ich kaufe deinen Eltern etwas Richtiges.
options.en: I will buy your parents something proper.
options.feedback: The screwdriver from the Brockenhaus cost eight francs and he still uses it. Price is not the axis here.
One at a time, everybody watching, an hour for nine people. Sitting through it is the participation.
No. Presents, then three hours of fondue. The order is not negotiable and nobody will explain it.
Somebody will. Asking is fine and the answer is already decided and nobody said so.

steps.speaker: Kurt
steps.es: Der ist von vor dem Krieg. Den gibt es heute nicht mehr.
steps.en: That is from before the war. They do not make those any more.

options.feedback: That is the longest sentence he will say all evening. It is also, from him, the whole thank you.

options.es: Ich habe ihn im Brockenhaus gefunden.
options.en: I found it in the Brockenhaus.
options.feedback: He will like that better than a shop. Say it plainly and stop.
He said two sentences about a screwdriver. Asking again makes him say a third, and he will not.

steps.speaker: Grossmutter
steps.es: Grau. Für einen Mann geht nur grau.
steps.en: Grey. For a man only grey will do.

options.en: Thank you very much. They are lovely.
options.feedback: She started them in October, before she had met you. That is the part the socks are actually about.
She did, and she has been waiting all evening for somebody to ask.
She is ninety-one, she has an opinion about wool, and this is not the moment to test it.
